claims.title: Nicarao and Chorotega settle the Pacific lowlands
claims.summary: Nahua-speaking Nicarao and Oto-Manguean Chorotega establish chiefdoms in western Nicaragua, farming the volcanic lowlands around Lakes Managua and Nicaragua.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Nicaragua: From the Nicarao and the colonial rival cities of León and Granada to a republic shaped by intervention, revolution, and contested power.", terralore.co/country/NIC/chronicle#ev-800-nicarao-and-chorotega-settle-the-pacific, claim TL:NIC:event:800:nicarao-and-chorotega-settle-the-pacific, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: First Spanish contact
claims.summary: The expedition of Gil González Dávila reaches the Pacific coast and encounters the Nicarao, opening the way to Spanish conquest.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Nicaragua: From the Nicarao and the colonial rival cities of León and Granada to a republic shaped by intervention, revolution, and contested power.", terralore.co/country/NIC/chronicle#ev-1522-first-spanish-contact, claim TL:NIC:event:1522:first-spanish-contact, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Founding of León and Granada
claims.summary: Francisco Hernández de Córdoba founds León and Granada, the rival cities whose Liberal and Conservative elites would shape Nicaraguan politics for generations.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Nicaragua: From the Nicarao and the colonial rival cities of León and Granada to a republic shaped by intervention, revolution, and contested power.", terralore.co/country/NIC/chronicle#ev-1524-founding-of-leon-and-granada, claim TL:NIC:event:1524:founding-of-leon-and-granada, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: León Viejo abandoned
claims.summary: The original León, struck by the Momotombo eruption of 1578 and the earthquake of 1610, is abandoned; its buried ruins later become Nicaragua's first UNESCO World Heritage Site.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Nicaragua: From the Nicarao and the colonial rival cities of León and Granada to a republic shaped by intervention, revolution, and contested power.", terralore.co/country/NIC/chronicle#ev-1610-leon-viejo-abandoned, claim TL:NIC:event:1610:leon-viejo-abandoned, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: British protectorate over the Mosquito Coast
claims.summary: Great Britain allies with the Miskito kings and treats the Caribbean Mosquito Coast as a protectorate, leaving the region distinct from Hispanic Pacific Nicaragua.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Nicaragua: From the Nicarao and the colonial rival cities of León and Granada to a republic shaped by intervention, revolution, and contested power.", terralore.co/country/NIC/chronicle#ev-1655-british-protectorate-over-the-mosquito-coast, claim TL:NIC:event:1655:british-protectorate-over-the-mosquito-coast, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Independence from Spain
claims.summary: Nicaragua, with the other provinces of the Captaincy General of Guatemala, declares independence from Spain in the Act of Independence of Central America.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Nicaragua: From the Nicarao and the colonial rival cities of León and Granada to a republic shaped by intervention, revolution, and contested power.", terralore.co/country/NIC/chronicle#ev-1821-independence-from-spain, claim TL:NIC:event:1821:independence-from-spain, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Separation from the Central American federation
claims.summary: Amid regional rivalry, Nicaragua withdraws from the Federal Republic of Central America to become a fully sovereign state.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Nicaragua: From the Nicarao and the colonial rival cities of León and Granada to a republic shaped by intervention, revolution, and contested power.", terralore.co/country/NIC/chronicle#ev-1838-separation-from-the-central-american-federation, claim TL:NIC:event:1838:separation-from-the-central-american-federation, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: William Walker's filibuster
claims.summary: Hired by León's Liberals, the American filibuster William Walker seizes Granada and makes himself president of Nicaragua in 1856 before a coalition of Central American states expels him.

sources.label: Territorial Expansion, Filibustering, and U.S. Interest in Central America
sources.publisher: U.S. Department of State, Office of the Historian

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Nicaragua: From the Nicarao and the colonial rival cities of León and Granada to a republic shaped by intervention, revolution, and contested power.", terralore.co/country/NIC/chronicle#ev-1855-william-walker-s-filibuster, claim TL:NIC:event:1855:william-walker-s-filibuster, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Treaty of Managua
claims.summary: Britain cedes its claims on the Caribbean coast to Nicaraguan sovereignty, creating a self-governing Mosquito Reserve.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Nicaragua: From the Nicarao and the colonial rival cities of León and Granada to a republic shaped by intervention, revolution, and contested power.", terralore.co/country/NIC/chronicle#ev-1860-treaty-of-managua, claim TL:NIC:event:1860:treaty-of-managua, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Incorporation of the Mosquito Coast
claims.summary: President José Santos Zelaya militarily incorporates the British-influenced Caribbean coast into the Nicaraguan state.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Nicaragua: From the Nicarao and the colonial rival cities of León and Granada to a republic shaped by intervention, revolution, and contested power.", terralore.co/country/NIC/chronicle#ev-1894-incorporation-of-the-mosquito-coast, claim TL:NIC:event:1894:incorporation-of-the-mosquito-coast, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: United States Marine occupation
claims.summary: US Marines are stationed in Nicaragua to support Conservative governments and oversee its finances, with only a brief interruption, until 1933.

sources.label: Territorial Expansion, Filibustering, and U.S. Interest in Central America
sources.publisher: U.S. Department of State, Office of the Historian

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Nicaragua: From the Nicarao and the colonial rival cities of León and Granada to a republic shaped by intervention, revolution, and contested power.", terralore.co/country/NIC/chronicle#ev-1912-united-states-marine-occupation, claim TL:NIC:event:1912:united-states-marine-occupation, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Sandino's resistance
claims.summary: Augusto César Sandino wages guerrilla war against the Marines and National Guard, becoming a hemispheric symbol of resistance to US intervention.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Nicaragua: From the Nicarao and the colonial rival cities of León and Granada to a republic shaped by intervention, revolution, and contested power.", terralore.co/country/NIC/chronicle#ev-1927-sandino-s-resistance, claim TL:NIC:event:1927:sandino-s-resistance, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Assassination of Sandino
claims.summary: Sandino is lured to Managua and murdered by National Guard officers under Anastasio Somoza García, opening the way to the Somoza dictatorship.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Nicaragua: From the Nicarao and the colonial rival cities of León and Granada to a republic shaped by intervention, revolution, and contested power.", terralore.co/country/NIC/chronicle#ev-1934-assassination-of-sandino, claim TL:NIC:event:1934:assassination-of-sandino, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Rise of the Somoza dynasty
claims.summary: Anastasio Somoza García seizes the presidency, founding a family dictatorship that, directly or through proxies, rules Nicaragua until 1979.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Nicaragua: From the Nicarao and the colonial rival cities of León and Granada to a republic shaped by intervention, revolution, and contested power.", terralore.co/country/NIC/chronicle#ev-1936-rise-of-the-somoza-dynasty, claim TL:NIC:event:1936:rise-of-the-somoza-dynasty, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Sandinista Revolution
claims.summary: The FSLN overthrows Anastasio Somoza Debayle, ending the dynasty; the insurrection is estimated to have cost about 50,000 lives.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Nicaragua: From the Nicarao and the colonial rival cities of León and Granada to a republic shaped by intervention, revolution, and contested power.", terralore.co/country/NIC/chronicle#ev-1979-sandinista-revolution, claim TL:NIC:event:1979:sandinista-revolution, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Contra war
claims.summary: The United States finances and arms the Contra insurgency against the Sandinista government; the war kills an estimated tens of thousands and devastates the economy. Casualty figures vary and are estimates.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Nicaragua: From the Nicarao and the colonial rival cities of León and Granada to a republic shaped by intervention, revolution, and contested power.", terralore.co/country/NIC/chronicle#ev-1980-the-contra-war, claim TL:NIC:event:1980:the-contra-war, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Esquipulas II peace accord
claims.summary: Central American presidents sign a regional peace plan committing to democratisation and an end to support for insurgencies.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Nicaragua: From the Nicarao and the colonial rival cities of León and Granada to a republic shaped by intervention, revolution, and contested power.", terralore.co/country/NIC/chronicle#ev-1987-esquipulas-ii-peace-accord, claim TL:NIC:event:1987:esquipulas-ii-peace-accord, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Chamorro defeats Ortega
claims.summary: Violeta Barrios de Chamorro wins the presidency for an opposition coalition; Ortega cedes power in a peaceful transfer that ends the war.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Nicaragua: From the Nicarao and the colonial rival cities of León and Granada to a republic shaped by intervention, revolution, and contested power.", terralore.co/country/NIC/chronicle#ev-1990-chamorro-defeats-ortega, claim TL:NIC:event:1990:chamorro-defeats-ortega, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Ortega returns to power
claims.summary: Having won the 2006 election, Daniel Ortega is inaugurated president again, beginning a long second period in office.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Nicaragua: From the Nicarao and the colonial rival cities of León and Granada to a republic shaped by intervention, revolution, and contested power.", terralore.co/country/NIC/chronicle#ev-2007-ortega-returns-to-power, claim TL:NIC:event:2007:ortega-returns-to-power, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Re-election limits removed
claims.summary: A 2009 court ruling and 2014 constitutional reform abolish term limits, enabling Ortega's continued re-election and the consolidation of FSLN control.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Nicaragua: From the Nicarao and the colonial rival cities of León and Granada to a republic shaped by intervention, revolution, and contested power.", terralore.co/country/NIC/chronicle#ev-2014-re-election-limits-removed, claim TL:NIC:event:2014:re-election-limits-removed, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The 2018 crisis
claims.summary: Protests against social-security cuts become a mass anti-government movement met with deadly force; the UN and IACHR document a death toll estimated upward of 300 (figures are estimates).

sources.label: Nicaragua: Human rights crisis demands action and accountability

claims.title: Contested re-election
claims.summary: Ortega wins a further term after leading opposition candidates are detained, in an election widely criticised internationally.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Nicaragua: From the Nicarao and the colonial rival cities of León and Granada to a republic shaped by intervention, revolution, and contested power.", terralore.co/country/NIC/chronicle#ev-2021-contested-re-election, claim TL:NIC:event:2021:contested-re-election, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.
